body: The orchestrator maintains ONE long-lived Copilot SDK session across all conversations and channels. Session ID is persisted to SQLite so it survives daemon restarts. Alternatives considered: per-conversation sessions (rejected — loses cross-channel context), per-channel sessions (rejected — SDK sessions are heavyweight ~400MB). Trade-off: model switching requires session invalidation and recreation since SDK doesn't support mid-session model changes.
title: Single persistent orchestrator session

body: All messages (from Telegram, TUI, API) are processed one at a time through a serial queue. The SDK session is not thread-safe — concurrent sendAndWait() calls would corrupt state. Queue includes per-message callbacks for streaming response deltas back to the originating UI. Session creation is coalesced via a shared promise to prevent duplicate sessions from concurrent callers.
title: Serial message queue for orchestrator

body: Workers are dispatched non-blocking — create_worker_session and send_to_worker return acknowledgment immediately while work runs in background. Results feed back via feedBackgroundResult() which re-enters the orchestrator queue as a system message. Workers auto-destroy after each task completion (~400MB freed per session). Max 5 concurrent workers enforced to prevent resource exhaustion. Each worker runs with approveAll=true (no interactive permission prompts).
title: Fire-and-forget worker dispatch

body: Real-time response streaming uses HTTP/1.1 Server-Sent Events, not WebSocket. SSE is simpler, works through corporate proxies, and the one-directional server→client flow fits the use case (messages submitted via separate POST /message). 20-second heartbeat pings keep connections alive. Each client gets a connectionId on subscribe which must be included in POST /message.
title: SSE over WebSocket for streaming

body: SUPERSEDED: The three-tier LLM classifier model router was removed. Model selection is now manual via /model command or switch_model tool. No automatic model tier selection.
title: Three-tier model routing with LLM classifier

body: When an orchestrator session is lost (crash, expiration, model switch), the last 10 conversation turns from SQLite are injected as silent context into the new session via a 60s sendAndWait() call tagged '[System: Session recovered]'. This prevents the user from losing conversational context without requiring full session persistence. Conversation log is bounded to 200 entries, pruned every 50 inserts, with messages over 500 chars truncated.
title: Session recovery via context injection

body: Workers are blocked from operating in directories containing credentials: .ssh, .gnupg, .aws, .azure, .kube, .docker, .npmrc, and similar. Path traversal protection uses path.resolve() comparison to prevent bypasses like '../.ssh'. Workers run with full tool approval (approveAll) so this directory-level block is the primary safety mechanism.
title: Sensitive directory blocking for workers

body: API authentication uses a single bearer token generated at first daemon startup and stored in ~/.attache/api-token with filesystem mode 0o600 (owner-read-only). Token is re-read from file on each API client call (daemon may create between attempts). Only /status endpoint is unauthenticated (used for health checks). No CORS headers since API is localhost-only (127.0.0.1).
title: Bearer token auth from file

body: Daemon shutdown uses a three-state machine: idle → warned → shutting_down. First Ctrl+C with active workers shows a warning and moves to 'warned'. Second Ctrl+C force-exits. A 3-second timeout force-exits regardless. Shutdown sequence: stop Telegram bot → destroy all workers (Promise.allSettled) → clear worker map → stop Copilot client → close SQLite → exit(0). Unhandled rejections log but keep daemon alive; uncaught exceptions trigger immediate shutdown.
title: Graceful shutdown three-state machine

body: Daemon restart spawns a detached child process with ATTACHE_RESTARTED=1 env var, then the parent exits. Detached spawn ensures the child survives parent death. The child detects the env var on startup and sends a 'back online' notification to Telegram. Restart is scheduled 1 second after the current response is delivered to give time for response delivery. Triggered by restart_attache() tool or POST /restart (500ms delay).
title: Daemon restart via detached child spawn

body: Key gotchas with the worker system: (1) Workers auto-destroy after EACH send_to_worker call — you cannot do multi-turn interactions with a single worker. (2) Worker state is in-memory only — all workers are lost on daemon restart. Database stores session IDs but session state doesn't persist. (3) If a worker crashes before .finally() executes, the session may leak (~400MB). SDK timeout eventually reaps these. (4) Cancelled workers suppress their feedBackgroundResult callback — no notification to user.
title: Workers are ephemeral — gotchas

body: SUPERSEDED: Router and classifier sessions were removed. Model switching no longer involves a classifier session. The orchestrator session invalidation on model change may still apply but the router context is obsolete.
title: Model switching invalidates orchestrator session

body: The daemon prioritizes staying alive: (1) Orchestrator retries 3x with exponential backoff (1s, 3s, 10s) for transient errors (timeout, disconnect, EPIPE, ECONNRESET). (2) Fatal session errors (closed/destroyed/disposed/invalid/expired) trigger session invalidation for recreation. (3) Health check every 30s detects dead client, triggers client reset + session invalidation. (4) Classifier failure falls back to 'standard' tier. (5) Response delivered to user FIRST, logging is best-effort. (6) Unhandled rejections logged but don't crash. (7) Skill/memory load failures continue without those features.
title: Error recovery and resilience patterns

body: SSE events use schema version 1 with four event types: session.connected (connectionId), orchestrator.message.delta (streaming chunk), orchestrator.message.complete (final text + routing metadata), orchestrator.message.cancelled. Events have both new names and legacy 'type' field for backwards compat. Routing metadata (model, tier, routerMode, overrideName) only attached to .complete events. Envelope uses spread pattern — data fields duplicated at root level for old clients.
title: Event protocol and SSE schema

body: By default (ATTACHE_SELF_EDIT disabled), the orchestrator system message includes a large warning block prohibiting workers from modifying Attache source code. Only user project files, local skills, user .env, and external files are allowed. Must start daemon with --self-edit flag (sets ATTACHE_SELF_EDIT=1) to remove this restriction. The CLI flag is processed in src/cli.ts before daemon import.
title: Self-edit protection mechanism

body: Database schema changes use a manual migration pattern in db.ts: detect missing column/constraint via try/catch or schema introspection, then migrate by renaming old table, creating new one with correct schema, copying data, dropping old. Example: conversation_log migration added 'system' to the role CHECK constraint. No migration framework — all inline. WAL mode enabled for concurrent reads during writes.
title: Database migration pattern
